reason: The plan can be built in time, but it is worth almost nothing and has defects. (1) VALUE. By R11S-2's own Monte Carlo, an early verbatim PORT with #37 beats SI with #37 on bronze: 0.84/0.89/0.93 against 0.80/0.83/0.87. SI wins only on silver (about +0.10) and when the port is late. The pair {SI, #37} puts the unmeasured insertion into BOTH files, so it drops the only insertion-free hedge (#38 now, PORT under v2). The MC does not model that correlation: it models the successor's gain as independent of ours, and C2 P(<0) is 0.10-0.15. Rough EV of SI over a port-only v2: P(trigger) 0.10-0.15 x P(a real successor passes the refusals) ~0.5 x ~+0.1 silver = ~+0.005-0.008 P(silver). Bronze gains nothing, or loses a little when the port goes in early. (2) RULES. The R8 wording in force (CONTEXT 16:49) asks for an honest LAB gate, a dummy and a new OK. On an unknown successor no lab gate can exist, and G1-G7 are mechanical only. The 09:03 P6 text rejected SI for 'new code after R8, unscored stack'. Building the code before R8 fixes only the first half. (3) THE PROXY PROVES NOTHING. I checked write_test_submission in code cell 5, whitespace/comment-normalised: x138 = HF v3 = 56a7f948b762, amanatar old = amanatar v10 = c6114b2c75d4 (V7 frozen-preset and V9 timing lines). So refusal (4) rejects amanatar-old, and the test 'HF v3 and amanatar-old pass' contradicts itself. The only base that passes is HF v3, which is x138 with the comments stripped (same code path, datasets, docker pin and T4; ext_biohub-harmonic-fusion-v3/NOTES.md). The HF v3 dry run just repeats the K2 dummies and tests no real transplant. (4) THE BYTE TEST FAILS AS WRITTEN. The cell-0 override header embeds '(tools/build_probe_kernel.py --base {a.base})' (build_probe_kernel.py l.2518-2523), and probe.json branches on a.base == 'x138' (l.2593). So '--base succ on exp56 gives bytes == exp58' cannot hold unless the tag is special-cased, and special-casing it weakens the test. What holds up: the finals stay sha-identical if the tool lives only behind the new --base succ path. G6's FF sha equality has a precedent (exp58ff 2/2 PASS, CONTEXT l.1827). The runtime (+0.85 h insertion +0.14 h lowrefine, 8.0/9.5 h fail-soft gates) fits 12 h. About 16 h remain before R8, which is enough.
fix: Do not build SI. Put the ~2-3 h into what gives the large effect: a port-only E10 v2 at >= 0.954 (R11S-3) and fast detection (R11S-6: checks every 3 h plus 29 Sep 06:00, and the scoreDescending rank flag from R11S-7 with a test). Tie order is submit time, so detection speed decides where PORT lands in its copy block. If the user still wants SI after seeing the insertion-hedge point: (a) the read table should prefer PORT on a public tie (SI only if public(SI) >= public(PORT) + 0.001); (b) fix the tests: amanatar-old is EXPECTED REFUSED (write_test_submission c6114b2c vs 56a7f948); the byte test compares exp58 modulo the one cell-0 tag line, or the succ path writes the tag of the base whose sha it matched; (c) state in CONTEXT that G1-G7 are mechanical only, and that the lab-gate clause of R8 is waived by the user's OK and not met; (d) add a mutant built from x138 with a changed cell-2 knob (the likely form of a 0.954-0.955 successor), which must pass. HF v3 alone tests nothing.
realistic_gain: About +0.005-0.008 P(silver) and ~0 P(bronze), possibly slightly negative when the port goes in early, over a port-only v2. It pays off only in the ~5-8% world where an actionable x138-family successor appears whose change is outside the anchors and outside write_test_submission. In the no-trigger world (~85-90%) the effect is 0, and the cost is ~2-3 h of tooling plus 3 GPU dummies.
